name: Botpress
summary: Botpress (Quebec, ~51-100 staff, $40M raised, $25M Series B June 2025) is an AI agent platform whose customer-support agents issue refunds and update accounts for clients in any sector. It is the strongest 'channel partner' candidate in the list: embedding White Circle controls would cover every customer's agents at once. It is also a possible competitor, since its own content already pitches 'guardrails' and a security suite, so the first call should find out whether guardrails are built in-house.
product: Agent Studio plus Autonomous Engine (LLM-reasoned agents that call tools and APIs, with fallback and escalation rules), AI-native Helpdesk, Knowledge Bases and Tables. Self-serve and enterprise; claims use by 35% of the Fortune 500 (company claim).

ai_usage.what: Customer-facing LLM agents built on its platform by thousands of customers; per the verified review, support agents that issue refunds and update accounts, with escalation rules and fallback logic.

customers: Not verified by name in this pass; Botpress claims 35% of the Fortune 500. Case-study logos (e.g. Super Dispatch) appear in a CX Network report.

funding.last_round: Series B ($25M, led by Framework Venture Partners)

headcount.growth_note: Series B proceeds earmarked for engineering, go-to-market and support expansion; offices in Montreal and Quebec City. No dated headcount series found.

news.title: Botpress secures $25M Series B to scale infrastructure for production-ready AI agents
Botpress publishes 'Chatbot Security Guide: Risks & Guardrails (2026)', positioning its security suite
CX Network report on AI agents for the helpdesk, with Botpress and guardrails as a theme

hiring_signals.role: Careers page lists no AI-safety or security role in extracted text (page content thin; roles load dynamically). Treat as unconfirmed.

compliance.eu_ai_act_exposure: As a provider/enabler of customer-facing agents with EU customers, plus deployer duties flowing to its customers (transparency, human oversight). Not confirmed in this pass whether Botpress publishes an AI Act position.
compliance.notes: Trust Center lists CCPA, DORA, GDPR, HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2, with pentest report available on request. Strong baseline, so the pitch is runtime behavior control, not certification.

why_now: Botpress closed a $25M Series B on 2025-06-23 to expand engineering and go-to-market, and by 2026-01-12 was publishing guardrail-and-security content for chatbot buyers. Its agents are tool-calling (refunds, account updates), and the Sept 2026 industry framing (NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform, 2026-09-28, citing agents circumventing app-layer controls) makes runtime control a live buying topic for platforms like this.
likely_pains: Prompt injection in customer-built support agents causing unauthorized refunds or account changes
Data leaking across tenants or end users through shared knowledge bases and tool outputs
Agents taking destructive or irreversible actions via the Autonomous Engine's tool calls
Abuse and token-drain on free and self-serve tiers
Brand-safety and hallucination incidents that its customers blame on the platform
Enterprise security reviews (HIPAA, DORA, GDPR) demanding evidence of runtime controls and audit logs per customer agent

metrics.hypothesis: Fewer agent incidents per customer, faster enterprise security-review close, and guardrails as a paid tier or margin line.

economic_buyer.hypothesis: Sylvain Perron (co-founder and CEO) for a platform/channel deal; CTO or product lead for an embed. A CISO was not found.

decision_criteria.hypothesis: Latency overhead, multi-tenant policy isolation, API fit with Agent Studio, price per call at its volume, EU/US residency.

decision_process.hypothesis: Product and engineering evaluation, then CEO sign-off on a partnership or resale; likely a pilot on one workflow.

paper_process.hypothesis: Partnership or reseller agreement plus DPA; SOC 2/HIPAA on both sides.

identify_pain.hypothesis: Customers' agents act on live systems and any injection or leak is attributed to Botpress; enterprise buyers ask for guardrail evidence.

champion.hypothesis: Head of product or engineering for agent safety; a trust/security lead if one exists. Unnamed so far.

competition.hypothesis: Possible in-house guardrails (its own content already claims them), plus Lakera, Protect AI, NVIDIA NeMo Guardrails, Guardrails AI and model-provider filters.

persona_angles.angle: Your customers' agents issue refunds and touch accounts, so one injected agent becomes your incident; could we show you a runtime layer you can offer every Botpress agent without building it yourselves?
How do you stop an Autonomous Engine agent from calling a destructive tool on a hostile prompt today, and what would a policy check in that call path cost you in latency?
When an enterprise security review asks for evidence of runtime controls on customer-built agents, what do you hand them beyond the SOC 2 report?
If guardrails shipped as a per-agent policy toggle in Agent Studio, which customers would turn it on first, and are you building that or buying it?
Your customers in regulated sectors carry deployer duties under the EU AI Act and DORA, so audit logs showing which policy fired per agent action could become a feature you sell.

risks: Competitor risk: Botpress already markets 'guardrails' and a security suite, and may build or acquire its own control layer; check before investing selling time.
Channel risk: a partnership is a longer, lower-control sale than a direct deal, and Botpress may want white-label pricing that compresses margin.
Buyer fit: Botpress is a platform, not an end deployer; direct value is limited to its own helpdesk and internal agents.
No named security or AI-safety leader found; entry point is the CEO or an unconfirmed engineering lead.
Evidence gaps: no AI incident, security hiring, or customer list verified in this pass (careers page extract was thin; security/guardrails URLs guessed returned 404).
Company is in Quebec/Canada; White Circle's EU/US regions may need a Canadian data-residency conversation.
